paper_title: Quantum Time-Space Tradeoff for Finding Multiple Collision Pairs
classifications: Theory of computation → Quantum complexity theory
statement: ▶ Conjecture 15. Any quantum algorithm for finding K disjoint collisions in a random function f : [M ] → [N ] with success probability 2/3 must satisfy a time-space tradeoff of T 2 S ≥ Ω(K 2 N ).
context: We conjecture that the optimal tradeoff for finding K collisions is T 2 S = Θ(K 2 N ), which would imply an optimal time-space tradeoff of T 2 S ≥ Ω(N e 2 ) for Element Distinctness. ▶ Conjecture 15. Any quantum algorithm for finding K disjoint collisions in a random function f : [M ] → [N ] with success probability 2/3 must satisfy a time-space tradeoff of T 2 S ≥ Ω(K 2 N ). ▶ Corollary 16. If Conjecture 15 is true, then any quantum algorithm for solving the Element Distinctness problem with success probability 2/3 must satisfy a time-space tradeoff of T 2 S ≥ Ω(N e 2 ). We describe a quantum algorithm that achieves the tradeoff of T 2 S ≤ O(K e 2 N ). In order to simplify the analysis, we do not require the collisions to be disjoint.
